title: On-demand manufacturing of arbitrary small molecules

concept.text: The proposed innovation is a programmable manufacturing system that accepts a digital description of a small molecule and produces an isolated, usable quantity with little target-specific process development. Its ambition is kilogram-to-tonne production across a broadly defined range of stable small molecules, with high material efficiency and reusable equipment. This remains a manufacturing goal; the supplied demonstrations establish narrower automated synthesis capabilities.

Existing modular approaches assemble molecules from prefabricated, protected building blocks through repeated coupling, deprotection and purification steps. Extending that idea into a general manufacturing platform would require a sufficiently broad set of compatible operations, or a planner that selects suitable operations for each target. The platform would also need to move materials, control reaction conditions, separate products from changing impurity mixtures and recover solvents. Documented machines already integrate heating, stirring, liquid handling, catch-and-release cartridges and solvent evaporation; efficient solvent recycling and manufacturing-scale generality are additional proposed capabilities.

Scope synthesis: accepting a digital structure would have to mean more than executing a recipe developed manually for that molecule. The intended capability includes translating a new structure into a workable manufacturing route while declaring the available feedstocks, reaction families, structural exclusions and required human intervention. Here, arbitrary expresses the ambition of broad programmability; it does not establish that every imaginable structure is stable, accessible or manufacturable under common conditions.

significance.text: The supplied studies describe small-molecule synthesis as typically customized, specialist-dependent and substantially manual. A reusable platform that reliably manufactured many different molecules would reduce the need to develop a separate synthesis and production process for each target. Its most direct consequences would be faster access to synthesized compounds and less target-specific manufacturing development, potentially widening who can explore molecular functions.

Conditional impact synthesis: universal computation is a useful analogy for programmable versatility—one platform serving many outputs. It does not prove chemical universality or imply uniform cost, speed or efficiency across molecules. If broad structural coverage, manufacturing scale and efficient material use were achieved together, the system would provide a major new way to make molecular matter. Success across a few reaction families would still be valuable, but would support a narrower claim.

Conditional downstream possibilities include more responsive supply of medicines, agrochemicals and functional materials, and discovery loops in which synthesis is less limiting. These outcomes also depend on purity, formulation, qualification, feedstock availability, throughput and subsequent testing. Manufacturing a drug molecule does not by itself supply a finished medicine, and faster synthesis does not guarantee that synthesis ceases to be the slowest discovery step. Prices below established petrochemical production for simple commodity molecules are a separate economic possibility, not an automatic consequence of programmability.

Disciplinary synthesis: much of the necessary bond-forming chemistry and building-block design belongs to organic chemistry. The chemical-engineering advance would be integrating reactions, separations, material handling, solvent recovery, control and scale-up into a reusable production system. Planning and adaptive control also overlap computational chemistry and automation. This entry's chemical-engineering identity therefore depends on the central advance being the manufacturing platform; a new reaction alone would represent a different contribution.

missing_breakthrough.text: The central unsolved capability in the proposed platform is making both reaction execution and product isolation generalize across changing targets at kilogram scale and above. The demonstrated block-assembly approach uses a bounded reaction repertoire and a common purification strategy, but substrate-dependent adjustments remain necessary. The 2025 study specifically reports occasions requiring modified coupling, deprotection or catch-and-release conditions. A general planner would have to select mutually compatible steps rather than assume that every building block works under one recipe.

Purification is a substantial engineering challenge because each target changes the desired product, intermediates, reagents and impurity mixture. The retained 2024 supplement documents a tetramer timing breakdown with a 10-minute first coupling and a 60-minute purification step. Its automated purification procedure also includes three 15 mL acetone reverse-elution portions followed by concentration. These details motivate attention to separation time and solvent handling, but they do not establish complete process-mass intensity or show that purification and solvent use dominate industrial performance.

Engineering synthesis: scale-up must preserve reaction performance, reliable material transfer and separation selectivity while accommodating different product properties and impurity profiles. High material efficiency also requires accounting for building-block preparation, protecting groups, purification consumables and solvent losses, rather than evaluating only the coupling step. Integrated recovery and reuse must work without contaminating subsequent runs or demanding a new separation train for each target. The supplied studies establish neither this combined performance nor a reliable development-time forecast; feasibility and timing remain uncertain.

current_state.text: Wang, Angello, Blair, Burke and colleagues reported Rapid automated iterative small-molecule synthesis in Nature Synthesis 3, 1031–1038, published 29 May 2024, DOI 10.1038/s44160-024-00558-w. The abstract reports an order-of-magnitude speed improvement over previous iterative systems, whose carbon–carbon bond-forming cycles had taken approximately a day. The improvements combine tetramethyl-MIDA boronates, rapid homogeneous Suzuki–Miyaura coupling and optimized catch-and-release purification cartridges. This is a reported advance within an iterative synthesis architecture, not evidence of arbitrary structural coverage.

The supplied review had access to a subscription-preview main-article page containing the abstract and to a separate retained supplement with experimental procedures and timing information. The supplement documents automated synthesis of tetramer 34 in 59% yield, giving 11.2 mg, with final column chromatography. Thus, the evidence extends beyond the abstract, although the full main article was not available in the reviewed material. The supplement's graphical spectra were not inspected. The publisher page also listed a correction whose contents were not supplied, leaving its relevance unresolved.

Tyrikos-Ergas and colleagues subsequently reported automated iterative N–C and C–C bond formation in Angewandte Chemie International Edition, published 30 June 2025, DOI 10.1002/anie.202509974. Their imatinib demonstration produced 2 mg after final HPLC purification, with no intermediate analysis or isolation during the automated sequence. This target involved three difficult couplings with heterocyclic building blocks and highly polar intermediates that challenged purification. The authors also describe remaining needs for modified coupling, deprotection and catch-and-release conditions, limiting any inference of a single recipe that works for all substrates.

The supplied review covered the 2025 article's full main narrative, but did not inspect its embedded figures or linked supporting document. Together, the dated reports establish automated modular synthesis with milligram-scale multistep products and meaningful advances in reaction and purification integration. They do not demonstrate arbitrary-molecule manufacturing at kilogram-to-tonne scale with high material efficiency. The supplied record contains no freshness search establishing the broader field's status as of 1 November 2026; that gap does not invalidate the reported 2024 and 2025 achievements or prove that no subsequent progress occurred.

completion_criteria.text: Proposed milestone, not an established standard: starting from digital structures never previously made on the platform, produce at least one kilogram of each of several structurally unrelated targets without manual hardware redesign between targets. Include a heterocycle-rich drug-like molecule to challenge both reaction compatibility and isolation. Predeclare the target-selection procedure and report available building blocks, prior platform knowledge, manual route development and any condition tuning, so that digital-input generality can be assessed. One optimized natural-product campaign would not meet this breadth requirement.
completion_criteria.label: Produce kilogram quantities of unrelated unseen targets without hardware redesign

completion_criteria.text: Proposed measurement requirements: report product identity, purity, isolated yield, elapsed time, throughput and process-mass intensity for each target. Define process-mass intensity as material input per mass of isolated product, with explicit treatment of water and recycled streams. Set a numerical material-efficiency acceptance threshold before testing and declare accounting boundaries that include building-block preparation, purification and solvent recovery. Merely reporting this metric would not establish high efficiency; the results must meet the declared threshold and expose tradeoffs between speed, yield, purity and material use.
completion_criteria.label: Report full process metrics and meet predeclared material-efficiency threshold

completion_criteria.text: Proposed reproducibility and boundary tests: repeat campaigns across independent runs and, where feasible, an independent site using documented equipment and procedures. Report failed targets, operator interventions, cartridge or equipment changes, carryover, solvent recovery and performance after switching products. State structural exclusions and operating limits explicitly. Passing a finite target panel would establish demonstrated breadth within those boundaries, not literal universality; tonne-scale operation, broader chemical coverage and competitive economics would require additional evidence.
completion_criteria.label: Reproduce campaigns independently and report failures and operating boundaries

related_concepts.text: Roster-based synthesis: CHE-04, Plant-scale molecular separations that can retire the hardest distillations, overlaps directly with the isolation and recovery requirements of CHE-10. CHE-04 concerns replacing demanding large-scale separations; CHE-10 requires separations that remain effective as products and impurity mixtures change. CHE-05, First-time-right scale-up of multiphase reactors, could help translate compatible reaction steps into reliable production, but successful reactor scale-up alone would not provide route planning or general product isolation. A universal recyclable solvent, mentioned in the research but not listed as a separate roster entry, could assist recovery and reuse without constituting the manufacturing platform.

Roster-based synthesis: CHE-01, Ambient nitrogen fixation at industrial rate, efficiency, and lifetime; CHE-02, High-yield direct oxidation of methane to methanol with dioxygen; CHE-03, Fossil-parity olefins and liquid fuels from carbon dioxide; and CHE-06, Direct solar manufacture of fuels and chemicals, each concern particular transformations, feedstocks or energy pathways. They could supply chemicals or process capabilities useful to molecular manufacturing. Their defining goals concern specified production pathways, whereas CHE-10 concerns switching among many molecular outputs on a reusable platform. Broad programmability would not by itself establish the rates, selectivity, durability or economics sought by those entries.

Roster-based synthesis: CHE-07, Closed-loop monomers from real mixed plastic waste, overlaps with feedstock recovery and material circularity, but focuses on recovering monomers from heterogeneous waste. CHE-08, Land-free staple calories from carbon dioxide and renewable energy, concerns food production, where nutritional suitability and production scale introduce distinct requirements. CHE-09, Direct air capture near the thermodynamic limit, at climate scale, could connect to carbon supply in a wider manufacturing system, but capturing atmospheric carbon dioxide does not establish its conversion into diverse molecules. These entries remain distinct from CHE-10 and from one another.

change_log.change: Preserved CHE-10 and its title while defining the innovation as a proposed integrated manufacturing platform.
change_log.reason: The dated demonstrations support relevant components, but do not establish the full breadth, scale and efficiency ambition.

change_log.change: Replaced universal claims about customized synthesis and multi-year process campaigns with the documented description of synthesis as typically customized and specialist-dependent.
change_log.reason: The supplied evidence does not establish those stronger baselines for every molecule or useful production quantity.

change_log.change: Retained the universal-computation analogy while limiting it to programmable versatility and separating direct benefits from downstream product and economic outcomes.
change_log.reason: Chemical breadth, finished-product supply, discovery bottlenecks and commodity economics require separate demonstrations.

change_log.change: Integrated reaction, purification, solvent handling, recovery and scale-up barriers without declaring purification and solvent use the dominant industrial obstacle.
change_log.reason: The reviewed timing and solvent-volume examples motivate concern but provide neither industrial comparisons nor complete material accounting.

change_log.change: Corrected the 2024 evidence description from abstract-only to a partial main article plus a separately retained experimental supplement.
change_log.reason: The review documents substantive procedures, timings and a 59% yield, 11.2 mg tetramer result in the supplement.

change_log.change: Preserved the 2024 speed improvement and 2025 2 mg imatinib result with their publication dates, purification qualifications and condition-dependent limitations.
change_log.reason: These are supported achievements that should remain distinct from projections about general manufacturing.

change_log.change: Replaced the field-wide assertion of absence with a statement about what the supplied studies demonstrate and an explicit freshness limitation.
change_log.reason: An empty freshness record cannot establish the field's status on 1 November 2026.

change_log.change: Expanded the proposed kilogram milestone to specify output per target, purity, timing, material-efficiency acceptance, accounting boundaries, human intervention and reproducibility.
change_log.reason: Yield and process-mass-intensity reporting alone cannot establish efficient, broadly programmable manufacturing.

change_log.change: Explained relationships with every other supplied roster entry without merging their identities.
change_log.reason: Shared reactions, separations, feedstocks or scale-up requirements do not make the innovations equivalent.

unresolved_issues: The supplied record does not establish progress across the broader field after the dated demonstrations or its status on 1 November 2026.
The contents and significance of the correction listed on the 2024 publisher page remain unknown.
The full 2024 main article, graphical spectra in its supplement, and the 2025 embedded figures and supporting document were not inspected in the supplied review.
The chemical domain intended by arbitrary small molecules remains to be defined, including structural exclusions, feedstock assumptions and acceptable target-specific development.
No numerical threshold or benchmark for high material efficiency is established, and the supplied evidence does not quantify complete process-mass intensity.
The relative industrial importance of reaction limitations, purification, solvent handling and other scale-up barriers remains unquantified.
Feasibility, development time, kilogram-to-tonne performance and competitive economics remain open; finite demonstrations could establish breadth but not literal universality.
